title: PostgreSQL Performance Engineering: Query Plans, Indexes & Faster Queries
concept: Make slow queries fast with evidence instead of guesses: measure a baseline, read EXPLAIN ANALYZE, compare estimated and actual rows, choose indexes for the query pattern and column order, remove N+1 queries and deep OFFSETs, rewrite reports, and weigh what every index costs.
description: An advanced course for backend developers whose database became the bottleneck. Every lesson starts from an incident on the CodeDev learning platform - a sign-in that went from 4 ms to 900 ms after a release, a course page that sent 120 queries, page 400 of the activity log timing out, an AI-suggested composite index that the planner never used, a nightly progress report that ran for 40 minutes, two updates waiting on each other - and fixes it with a plan you can read: baselines and pg_stat_statements, EXPLAIN ANALYZE nodes and costs, statistics and selectivity, indexes per query pattern, the Query Got Slower scenario, composite index order, N+1, keyset pagination, report rewrites, lock contention and index trade-offs. 12 lessons with True/False quizzes on real plans and logs; the SQL challenges run on SQLite in the code runner and check results and query plans.

learningOutcomes.text: Measure a baseline and read execution plans: nodes, costs, estimated versus actual rows
Choose indexes for a query pattern, including expression indexes and composite column order
Remove N+1 queries and deep OFFSETs with joins and keyset pagination
Use statistics and selectivity to predict what the planner will do
Find lock contention and weigh the write and storage cost of every index

testedVersions.SQLite: sqlite3 module of the code runner's python3 (challenges)

knownIssues: The code runner has SQLite, not PostgreSQL: challenges check results and SQLite's EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN; lessons teach PostgreSQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE and note where SQLite differs

Choosing an index for the query pattern
